name: ALT
note: Health-based cut-off (95th percentile in healthy-weight adolescents; AASLD applies it from age 10), not the laboratory's reference interval. Under 10 years: no validated cut-off. The app reads ALT against the laboratory range under 11 years and against these limits from 11 years.

name: AST
note: CALIPER example (one analyzer, Abbott ARCHITECT; healthy community children and well outpatients, Toronto; ages in completed years). Use your laboratory's range first; the ULN calculator does not use these rows. Assay without pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (P5P); P5P assays read higher. AST also comes from muscle and red cells.

name: GGT
note: CALIPER example (one analyzer, Abbott ARCHITECT; healthy community children and well outpatients, Toronto; ages in completed years). Use your laboratory's range first; the ULN calculator does not use these rows. In a cholestatic infant, "low GGT" means low for the degree of cholestasis, not below this interval. Pale stools go to the biliary atresia pathway whatever the GGT.

name: ALP
note: CALIPER example (one analyzer, Abbott ARCHITECT; healthy community children and well outpatients, Toronto; ages in completed years). Use your laboratory's range first; the ULN calculator does not use these rows. ALP follows bone growth: highest in infancy and puberty; boys stay high longer.

name: AFP
note: Term infants, 95.5% interval (one center, older assay; infants with liver disease or neonatal jaundice excluded). Preterm infants run much higher. Adult levels (0–6 ng/mL) are not reached by age 2. Check the unit: some laboratories report IU/mL. Follow the trend, not one value.

name: Ammonia
note: Beyond the newborn period. Newborns: no guideline upper limit; definitions of hyperammonemia range from > 80 (Savy 2018) to > 110 µmol/L (Spanish consensus 2022). In a sick newborn, treat any value above your laboratory's range as abnormal and repeat at once. Falsely high with a tourniquet, crying, a capillary sample or a delayed, warm sample.
